concept.name: High price
concept.definition: The high price is the highest price at which any trade executed during a given period. It marks the upper extreme of the period's traded range and forms the top of an OHLC bar or candlestick wick.
concept.intuition: The high is the most anyone paid during the period — the peak of the price excursion.
concept.mechanics: Computed as the maximum of all executed trade prices within the aggregation interval; in charting it is rendered as the top of the vertical line (OHLC bar) or the upper shadow (candlestick).
concept.formula: H = max(p_i) over all trades i in the period.
concept.failure_modes: A single outlier or erroneous print (bad tick) can set a spurious high that distorts range-based indicators and stop levels; data vendors apply filters, but conventions differ. The high says nothing about how long price stayed near it.
concept.misconceptions: The high is not a resistance level by construction — it is just the maximum print; treating it as meaningful support/resistance requires additional analysis.
concept.example: If a stock trades between $50.10 and $51.80 during the day, the daily high is $51.80 even if only one lot traded there.
